Resolves #22027

Learn section links now reveal the requested heading and select the same entry in the existing **On this page** panel. The article and its section records publish together before the route jump. Clicking a contents entry and opening its URL use the same immediate heading alignment. Browser scroll anchoring keeps the heading in place when content above it expands. Learn’s contents observer selects one active heading using the article’s current reading position. Clearing an anchor or opening an unknown one resets the current article to the top and selects its first heading when it has one.

Evidence: L3 (normal Portal entry in headless Chromium) → L3 required (AC-1 through AC-3).

CI jobs: +0.

## AC Evidence

| Criterion | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| AC-1 | The existing Learn link suite now drives the actual Decision 3 link and a direct visit. Both assert the heading is fully in view and that the exact right-panel row is selected. The link-click test also scrolls to Decision 4 and confirms the highlight follows the reader. The browser measured the heading at Y 58.08 px in a reading area starting at Y 58 px. |
| AC-2 | The browser spec covers a fragment-only jump, plain and unknown fragment resets without a second fetch, sidebar navigation through late layout expansion, and the title selection after manual scroll back to the top. |
| AC-3 | The browser spec holds the old adoption guide response until the newer guide renders. It awaits the superseded request’s App Worker lifecycle and checks the newer article, both sets of contents records (Worker and DOM), and its scroll position. |

## Deltas from ticket

The updated ticket records the contents-panel selection and stale-list requirements. Route fragments resolve through the same section records the panel already displays. Heading anchors now come from Marked’s text renderer and a character allowlist, while Marked’s normal renderer produces the displayed heading.

## Test Evidence

All 12 Learn routing cases passed in headless Chromium, and all 54 focused unit cases passed. The committed slug test covers inline code, link text, entity markup, duplicate anchors, and an article without headings. An earlier real Mermaid probe held its module until after the click, then expanded the article by 1,190 px above the target. The heading and right-hand selection held at normal speed and under 5× CPU slowdown. The frame pair shows the same direct URL at 1440 × 900 before and after.

| ![The article starts at its title while the URL points to Decision 3](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/9338799d3c65963700fae3fd1acf838ac8a7a7aa/review-evidence/22027/decision-3-before.jpg?raw=true) | ![Decision 3 is in view and its right-hand contents entry is selected](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/9338799d3c65963700fae3fd1acf838ac8a7a7aa/review-evidence/22027/decision-3-after.jpg?raw=true) |

Frame critique: The heading starts at the article’s top edge and its selection is visible in the existing right-hand panel. Long section names wrap inside that panel.
